title: Binary time classes under alphabet encoding
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let $e:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an injective map, let $L$ be a language of finite binary words, and let $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$. If a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, on each input obtained by applying $e$ symbolwise to a binary word $x$, halts within $T(|x|)$ steps and outputs the one-symbol encoding under $e$ of the indicator of whether $x\in L$, then $L$ belongs to $\mathrm{DTIME}(n\mapsto T(n)+1)$.
hypotheses_covered: e is an injective embedding of the binary alphabet into Γ
L is a language of binary words
T is a natural-number-valued time bound
A finite Turing machine over Γ decides L via e within T
replaced:
Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, let
$e : \{0,1\} \hookrightarrow \Gamma$ be an injective embedding of the binary
symbols, let $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^{*}$ be a language over the binary alphabet,
and let $T : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{N}$ be a time bound. If some deterministic
finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$ decides $L$ via $e$ within time $T$, then
$L \in \mathrm{DTIME}(n \mapsto T(n) + 1)$; that is, some deterministic finite
Turing machine over the binary alphabet decides $L$ within
$a \cdot (T(n) + 1)$ steps on every input of length $n$, for some constant $a$.
